PullRequest.Title: Stop ABExp.queriedFeature telemetry from being redacted as a file path
PullRequest.Body:
### Summary

The new TAS assignments endpoint (POST /api/v1/assignments) returns every feature variable key scoped with a `/vscode/` prefix (e.g. /vscode/config.foo). The telemetry cleaner's anonymizeFilePaths heuristic treats any word/word value as a path and redacts it, making the field `ABExp.queriedFeature` unusable for "which feature is being experimented on" queries.

**Fix**
Mark `ABExp.queriedFeature` as a trusted telemetry value in both experiment-telemetry sinks so cleanData skips path anonymization for it (the field is always an experiment feature key, never user data). This preserves the raw name — the redaction disappears and the field is queryable again.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and configuration refresh resolving experiment-backed settings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold start, the first treatment request awaits the shared TAS client initialization and initial fetch; subsequent setting reads use the populated in-memory client. Telemetry payload cleaning and appender dispatch happen synchronously after each treatment result but the diff only changes how one already-present property is represented.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch legacy/new TAS assignments used by all treatment reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced initial fetch per TAS client generation, plus existing timer/filter-driven refetches; not one fetch per queried setting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same TAS initialization, assignments request, cache, and refetch behavior existed before the payload-wrapping change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The cold first treatment waits for initialFetch; warm reads do not cross this network boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward each cleaned telemetry event to telemetry appenders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing appender call per emitted query event per configured IPC appender; scoped lookup can avoid the bare fallback, while a miss can cause a second tas-client query event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each query event already traversed publicLog, cleaning, and appender dispatch; the diff adds no event or appender call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget channel dispatch occurs after treatment resolution and does not gate returning the treatment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue the existing cleaned event in the telemetry SDK for backend transmission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged one tracked event per emitted query event and configured 1DS appender; SDK transport batching is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same telemetry event and transport path existed; only ABExp.queriedFeature now bypasses string-cleaning regexes via TelemetryTrustedValue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tracking is invoked synchronously, but transport is not awaited by treatment resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with the number of experiment-backed configuration properties processed and with scoped-key fallback misses. The diff preserves the existing O(number of telemetry properties) copy and adds only one constant-time conditional/object allocation for the matching property; it may avoid regex cleaning of that string.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Experimental settings are processed sequentially by processExperimentalSettings. All cold treatment reads share the same tasClient/initialFetch promise, so there is one effective initial assignment fetch rather than one network request per setting. Telemetry dispatch remains one postEvent path per tas-client query with the existing appender fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold treatment access awaits the shared initial fetch; warm accesses read the TAS client's in-memory assignments. Client replacement resets that cache generation, while normal feature-query telemetry is not cached or coalesced. The changed trusted wrapper neither changes TAS cache keys nor negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed helper, treatment callers, shared initial-fetch promise, cleaner, IPC client, and telemetry appender path were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of registered experiment-backed settings and configured telemetry appenders varies by product build, but neither cardinality nor concurrency is changed by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The runtime loop and telemetry boundaries already existed; marking one value trusted adds bounded constant work and skips cleaner regex work without increasing calls, retained state, or critical-path I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub Copilot extension reading TAS feature variables and emitting query telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Treatment reads synchronously consult the initialized delegate's in-memory assignments, first using the /vscode/-scoped key and then the bare key on a miss. The tas-client query telemetry then traverses BaseTelemetryService.postEvent and existing Microsoft reporters; initial assignment fetching is managed separately by the delegate and is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize/refetch TAS assignments used by feature reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial fetch per delegate generation plus existing polling/filter-driven refreshes, shared by feature lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Delegate creation, caching, and assignment network requests are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization can gate callers that explicitly await hasTreatments, but ordinary getTreatmentVariable reads are in-memory; the changed postEvent logic does not move assignment fetching onto either path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue the existing query event to external Microsoft telemetry and, for internal users, the existing raw internal reporter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged one external sender call per query event and at most one additional internal sender call for internal users; scoped misses may already produce an additional query event through the bare lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both sender calls and their destination fan-out existed before the PR. The change only wraps the already-present queried-feature string before those calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter methods are invoked synchronously but no promise is awaited by the feature read; transport remains off the read's awaited critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of feature-variable reads and scoped-key misses. Per emitted event, the diff adds one property lookup, type check, and short-lived wrapper allocation; payload size and sender count remain unchanged, while downstream cleaning can skip work for that value.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each caller performs synchronous in-memory reads. Delegate initialization/refetch owns the existing network concurrency. postEvent keeps its existing two sender invocations: the internal reporter is a no-op for non-internal users, while the external reporter queues the event; the PR adds no parallel request or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Assignments are cached in the tas-client delegate and shared across feature reads. Scoped and bare names remain distinct lookup keys, with bare fallback only on a scoped miss. Query telemetry itself remains uncached. The trusted-value object is event-local and not retained.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed postEvent method, scoped fallback, delegate cache lifecycle, reporter construction, and sender fan-out were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact query frequency varies with enabled Copilot features and account type, but the added work is constant and event-local even at high lookup counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is no new network/IPC boundary, concurrency burst, retained collection, or scaling payload transformation; the constant wrapper allocation is not actionable and can reduce cleaner CPU.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. Traced workbench and Copilot TAS query paths through caches, payload cleaning, IPC/reporters, and network appenders. The PR preserves event and boundary cardinality and adds only bounded trusted-value wrapping, so no performance finding was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
